sentences.text: 2 2. What is under challenge is the validity of the analysis report of the Food Inspector involved in S.T.No.108/2012 of the Chief Judicial Magistrate's Court, Ernakulam.

3. Relying on the decision reported in Pepsico India Holdings Pvt. Ltd. v. Food Inspector and another [2010(4) KLT 706(SC)], this Court in Gopalakrishnan v. Food Inspector[2013(3) KLT 455]
had held that the decision in Pepsico(supra) that the provisions under Section 23(1A)(ee) and (hh)
of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act are mandatory and the same are applicable to all the food items.

entities.text: Pepsico India Holdings Pvt. Ltd. v. Food Inspector and another [2010(4) KLT 706(SC)]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 4. The question involved in this case is the non- compliance of the mandatory provisions contained under Section 23(1A)(ee) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act.
As there was a divergent view in the matter, the decision in Gopalakrishnan(supra) along with the other decisions of the learned Single Judges were referred to the Division Bench.

The Division Bench of this Court in Crl.R.P.No.1814/2002 considered the said question and has disposed of the matter through order dated 17.11.2015 thereby upholding the view taken by this Court in Gopalakrishnan(supra).
5.

Matters being so, the continued prosecution of the petitioners in S.T.No.108/2012 of the Chief Judicial Magistrate's Court, Ernakulam are illegal and no purpose would be served in proceeding with the matter any further.
The matters involved in the said case are quite unnecessary in view of the decisions noted supra and therefore, the same are liable to be quashed.

In the result, this Crl.M.C. is allowed and Annexure No.I complaint on the basis of Annexure No.II Report and all further proceedings initiated against the petitioners in S.T.No.108/12 of the Chief Judicial Magistrate's Court, Ernakulam, are hereby quashed.
Sd/- B. KEMAL PASHA, JUDGE.
